CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, MAY 27, 2025

CALL TO ORDER  Maria Davila, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at
  6:36 p.m.

INVOCATION  Pastor Raul Flores, Ministerio Monte De Alabanza

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  Luis Frausto, Director of Administrative Services
ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Maria Davila, Vice Mayor Joshua Barron, Council Member Maria
  del Pilar Avalos, Council Member Gil Hurtado and Council Member Al
  Rios; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager Rob Houston, City
  Attorney Raúl F. Salinas

1
CITY COUNCIL
APPOINTMENTS  The City Council ratified the appointment by Council Member Maria del
  Pilar Avalos of Margarita Valenzuela to the Planning Commission by
  motion of Council Member Avalos and seconded by Council Member
  Hurtado.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila,
  yes.

2
STREETS/SIDEWALKS/
LANDSCAPING  Following the conclusion of the public hearing, the City Council
  unanimously adopted Resolution No. 2025-16-CC entitled Resolution of
  the City Council of the City of South Gate, California, ordering the levy of
  the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Annual Assessment for the Street Lighting and
  Landscaping Maintenance District No. 1, by motion of Council Member
  Avalos and seconded by Council Member Hurtado.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila,
  yes.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025

3
TRACT MAP ADMIN  Following the conclusion of the public hearing, the City Council
  unanimously approved items A & B (as amended) by motion of Council
  Member Avalos and seconded by Vice Mayor Barron:

  a. Determining that in accordance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act (“CEQA”), the project qualifies for a categorical
  exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15332, (Class 32) “In-Fill
  Development Projects”, and is thereby exempt from CEQA. The
  project site is surrounded by urban uses and the proposed residential
  condominium subdivision will be compatible with surrounding
  existing development.

  b. Resolution No. 2025-17-CC entitled Resolution of the City Council of
  the City of South Gate, California, upholding the action of the
  Planning Commission to approve Vesting Tentative Tract Map No.
  84531 to allow the subdivision of one parcel into a 54-unit residential
  condominium development located at 10130 Adella Avenue, within the
  Industrial Flex (IF) zone in the Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan, and
  finding the action categorically exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act Guidelines.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Rios, no; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila,
  yes.

  City Attorney Salinas stated this hearing is much like an administrative
  proceeding and instead of having a judge, we have the five City Council
  Members that will be making the decision. But like in court, it’s important
  to allow for the presentations to be made. It’s important for everyone to
  listen to the presentations. People may say things you do not agree with,
  but it’s important that you refrain from commenting on those other than at
  the time when you come to the microphone.

  City Manager Houston explained the proceeding of the public hearing,
  with City Staff giving an overview of the project first, then the Appellant
  will give their presentation and then the developer. At the close of the
  presentations the public comment period will open.

  Gabriel Perez, Director of Community Development stated Senior
  Planner, Rodrigo Pelayo, is going to be giving the presentation.

  Rodrigo Pelayo, Senior Planner gave the presentation.

  City Manager Houston explained that the state has mandated on how
  many new housing units need to be available in communities.

  Page 2 of 16
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025

3
TRACT MAP ADMIN
CONT’D
  Council Member Avalos asked for clarification on 50,000 per unit of bad
  faith which comes out to be $2.7 million dollars of the general fund that
  the city would have to pay.

  Mr. Pelayo stated that is correct.

  City Manager Houston stated in discussions with the developer and
  neighborhood, we have been trying to talk about different alternatives for
  the K-rail and the gate. The city has been willing to withdraw condition 60
  and offer to allow the K-rail to remain and not be part of this project.

  Appellants, Jose Morales and his wife, Beatrice Morales, 5343 Almira
  Rd., on behalf of South Gate Progress Partners, are asking the Council to
  reconsider parts of this project, specifically the removal of the K-rail
  barrier and environmental concerns. This is not about stopping housing,
  but making sure it’s done responsibly.

  Mr. Morales asked Mrs. Morales to expand on these concerns.

  Mrs. Morales’ presentation was not audible.

  Developer, Nick Patterson (City Ventures) on behalf of South Gate 1
  Investments, LLC, the presentation was not audible. Mr. Patterson asked
  the legal consultant Chris Burt from Cox Castle & Nicholson, LLP to
  speak.

  Chris Burt from Cox Castle & Nicholson is Land Use Counsel for the
  Applicant forwarded two letters over the weekend responding to
  allegations in the appeal.

  Mr. Burt addressed Condition No. 60, and the applicant supports the K-rail
  barrier remain. He also addressed concerns regarding contamination.

  Mr. Salinas asked Mr. Burt to respond to one of the appeals a little more
  thoroughly regarding a full-blown environmental analysis is required as
  it’s being suggested by the appellant.

  Mr. Burt stated that a full-blown environmental analysis is not accurate as
  it was explained in the letter. He proceeded to explain.

  Mr. Salinas stated that another issue raised was vaper intrusion and to
  please explain.

  Mr. Burt will explain but might need Stan to speak on VIMS (Vapor
  Intrusion Mitigation Systems) which are common throughout Southern

  Page 3 of 16
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025

3
TRACT MAP ADMIN
CONT’D  California for sites that have a history of remediation or past
  contamination.

  Mr. Salinas asked if he has heard about the state laws and the fact that this
  is subject to the Housing Act that was passed in Sacramento. If he can
  comment upon that law and how it impacts the decision-making authority
  of this council?

  Mr. Burt stated staff did an excellent job of summarizing what the
  Housing Accountability Act says. He is not here to opine what Sacramento
  does versus local control. The state of the law on Housing Accountability
  Act limits the ability of local agencies to deny housing projects that are
  consistent with objective standards.

  Josh Sargent with Stantec Consulting, a professional geologist in the state
  of California, explained the VIMS system.

  Mr. Salinas asked if a resident living next door to the town home, when
  these vapors come up, do they come up near the residents’ homes.

  Mr. Sargent stated they’ll be coming up through the site and they will be
  mitigated through the installation of a vapor intrusion mitigation system.

  Mr. Salinas asked Mr. Sargent to explain in plain laymen’s words what
  VIMS is.

  Mr. Sargent stated that the VIMS is a multi-layer system and explained the
  procedure.

  Mr. Salinas stated the City Council may have additional questions. He was
  asking for clarification for the benefit of the public.

  Councilwoman Avalos thanked Mr. Sargent for his explanation and asked
  if the VIMS been put in place or will they be put in prior to the
  construction.

  Mr. Sargent stated the VIMS has not been done. It is in connection with
  the building construction.

  Mayor Davila asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on this
  item.

  Mario Dominguez is in support of building town homes and if the
  residents are requesting that the K-rail remain, then it should stay.

  Page 4 of 16
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025
3
TRACT MAP ADMIN
CONT’D  Issues discussed involved the K-rail barrier on Adella Avenue, traffic and
  environmental concerns:

  Marissa Delgado, 5305 Aldrich; Natalie, 10334 Blumont Rd.

  Rob Houston, City Manager, mentioned before the presentations and he
  reemphasized that the K-rail will not be removed.

  Continuation on the issues discussion involving the K-rail barrier on
  Adella Avenue, traffic and environmental concerns:

  Rosanna La Rosa resides south of the project; Susan Janer, 5314 Batavia
  Rd.; Patricia Navarro, 5317 Almira Rd., and member of the South Gate
  Progress Partners; Ignacio Uribe; Miriam Mendez, Aldrich Rd.; Javier,
  South Gate resident.

RECESS  The City Council recessed at 8:01 p.m., and reconvened at 8:10 p.m., with
  all Members of Council present.

  Continuation on the issues discussion involving the K-rail barrier on
  Adella Avenue, traffic and environmental concerns:
  Christina Navarro, Batavia Rd.; Alma Ruvalcaba, Almira Rd.; Daniela
  Casanorsano, 5217 Batavia Rd.; Luis, South Gate resident for 16-years;
  Darla Castellanos, Aldrich; Luis Martiz, South Gate resident for 35-years;
  Maribel, Almira Rd.; Melanie Franco; Robert Ramirez, South Gate
  resident for 10-years; Lizette, Almira Rd.; Hilda, Batavia Rd.; Lupe
  resides in area 4; Stephanie; Alicia Gonzalez, Batavia Rd.

  Emails regarding the continuation of the issues discussed involving the K-
  rail barrier on Adella Avenue, traffic and environmental concerns:
  Stephanie Pimentel, member of the South Gate Progress Partners; January
  Bonilla, Gladys Bonilla, Yadira Bonilla-Clayton and Alvaro Bonilla stated
  their neighborhood known as manor has been their home for the family
  since 1976; Carlos Gallegos, member of South Gate Progress; Caroline
  Gonzalez, Eric Gonzalez, Eric Gonzalez, Jr., Ethan Gonzalez and Jose
  Jesus Gonzalez.

  Dylan Cassie on behalf of the California Housing Defense Fund urges the
  City of South Gate to comply with state housing laws.

  Y. Law urges the City of South Gate to comply with state housing laws
  including the housing accountability act.

  Having no one else come forward nor any emails, Mayor Davila closed
  the audience portion.

  Page 5 of 16
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025

3
TRACT MAP ADMIN
CONT’D  Mr. Salinas stated the appellant may make any closing remarks and then
  the applicant.

  Mr. Morales thanked City Council Members for listening to everyone’s
  comments and his neighbors’ for attending tonight’s meeting. He is asking
  not to rush and decide tonight.

  Mrs. Morales echoed her husband’s comments. Thank everyone for their
  time and dedication.

  Developer, Nick Patterson (City Ventures) on behalf of South Gate 1
  Investments, LLC, thanked everyone for their time and attending tonight’s
  meeting. They have been working well together and are excited to
  continue with this project. He addressed a few comments brought up
  during public comments.

  Chris Burt from Cox Castle & Nicholson, LLP commented on the traffic
  comments brought up during public comments. He also stated the site is
  clean after removing tons and tons of soil and replaced with clean soil.
  There were additional studies and site assessments that were delivered to
  the fire department. The fire department concluded that no additional
  remediation on site was required to make the site safe for human
  habitation or housing. He also explained the reason for VIMS.

  Josh Sargent with Stantec Consulting thanked everyone for providing
  comments this evening. He answered the comments.

  Mr. Salinas stated there was a representation made by the developer that
  an agreement was reached with the appellant regarding Condition No. 60.
  He asked that issue be addressed by both parties.

  Mr. Burt stated they reached out to the appellants maybe two weeks ago
  shortly after the appeal was filed to learn of their concerns with respect to
  the project.

  Mr. Morales stated today was the first time after listening to the City
  Manager that the city is willing to remove the condition altogether. As far
  as modification to the Condition, we would still need to discuss the
  language.

  Mr. Houston asked for Condition 60 to be pulled up regarding the K-rail.
  Other parts of the 60 would be retained. The city is proposing to remove
  the language regarding the unit’s design installation.

  Mr. Patterson stated that after the Planning Commission approval on
  March 18, 2025, a traffic study was completed.

  Page 6 of 16
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025

3
TRACT MAP ADMIN
CONT’D  Mayor Davila asked when the study was done.

  Mr. Patterson believes the study was completed on May 19, 2025.

  Council Member Hurtado stated LAUSD through eminent domain-built
  schools that are impacting those areas, and the city could not prohibit it
  from happening. He also mentions that the state is expecting cities to build
  more housing units, or the cities get fined if they don’t comply. He
  thanked all the speakers present tonight.

  Council Member Hurtado asked how many parking spaces will be
  available.

  Mr. Patterson responded with 108 parking spaces when counting the two-
  car garage.

  Council Member Hurtado asked if more parking spaces can be added. Mr.
  Patterson stated that the way the site is currently laid out and with certain
  restrictions on the buildings it cannot and the trash closures that are at the
  end of every driving aisle.

  Council Member Hurtado understands the K-rail will remain but would
  like something else permanent.

  Mr. Burt stated as to the applicant’s perspective the concept of something
  more permanent being there they do not object to, but the idea that the
  applicant be required to construct and fund a replacement is a concern.

  Council Member Hurtado understands but both sides need to be
  considered.

  Mr. Burt believes the residents are okay with the K-rail to remain.

  Council Member Rios thanked South Gate manor for attending tonight’s
  meeting. He is concerned about the traffic and believes an emergency
  entry/exit is needed for emergency vehicles to have access.

  Council Member Rios asked what company was on that site that made the
  parcel contaminated.

  Mr. Salinas mentioned when LAUSD bought the property it was
  discovered chromium was present from a manufacturing plant.

  Council Member Rios understands the public’s concerns to have
  environmental reports done before construction, not after.

  Page 7 of 16
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025

RECESS  The City Council recessed at 9:39 p.m., and reconvened at 9:48 p.m., with
  all Members of Council present.

3
TRACT MAP ADMIN
CONT’D  Council Member Avalos thanked Mr. & Mrs. Morales for bringing this
  issue to the attention of the Council. She mentioned traveling to
  Sacramento and spoke with the legislators regarding the issue of building
  housing in a high-density city. The reply was to build up. She would have
  liked the communities to have gotten together and fought this state law.

  Council Member Avalos thanked City Ventures for working with the
  community.

  Mayor Davila is also disappointed with the legislators passing the Housing
  Act.

  Vice Mayor Barron questioned the $2.7 million the state can fine the city
  and approve the housing project regardless of what the Councils’ decision.

  Vice Mayor Barron asked the developer regarding the contamination and
  what is the required footing for a three-story building.

  Mr. Sargent stated that the soil contamination at the property has been
  removed. He mentioned a little bit of lead at the property line on the north
  side.

  Vice Mayor Barron asked Rodrigo Pelayo about the required footing for a
  three-story building.

  Mr. Pelayo cannot answer his question because the planning division
  reviewed conceptual plans, and they don’t get into that level of detail.

  Mr. Patterson stated that the foundations are still being calculated. They
  are going through their construction documents. The standard slab would
  be between 12 and 24 inches.

  Vice Mayor Barron wanted to make certain everyone is fine with the K-
  rail. He was under the impression the community deserved something
  better than a K-rail.

  Councilwoman Avalos asked City Manager if it would be possible to
  provide the community with parking permits at no cost due to this
  development.

  Mr. Houston stated that is something to consider, but we want to be
  cautious about precedence, and it is not on the agenda for discussion.

  Page 8 of 16
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025

3
TRACT MAP ADMIN
CONT’D  Council Member Hurtado asked the City Manager and City Attorney if the
  city can be fined for not approving a project. Does that still apply if the
  Council puts certain conditions to this project and the developer decide to
  walk away.

  Mr. Salinas stated that under the statute, it’s regulated by HCD, which is a
  state agency, the city runs the risk of being fined if there are conditions
  being imposed that fall outside of the very strict parameters that the state
  has said the city can consider. He will have the developer’s attorney speak
  on this issue.

  Mr. Burt gave the Council an explanation.

  Council Member Hurtado understands and is not trying to put conditions
  on the developer, but the project is creating an adverse condition to the
  residents.

  Council Member Hurtado asked since the K-rail has been placed how
  many times have we had a need for emergency services to go through.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer, stated once within the last two years.

  Mayor Davila asked Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works, to speak
  about several traffic studies done in that area.

  Mr. Cervantes stated the major arterials are impacted by regional traffic.
  The Atlantic by Tweedy area is an impact area. The city has looked at the
  area as a whole with what exists today and the potential for future impacts
  as well. The city has come up with an Atlantic Corridor Plan with the
  COG. The city has done traffic studies for the school, junior high school.
  The Public Works Department is requiring a traffic study for this project.
  The developer has prepared a traffic study. The city does have its own
  traffic study requirements. First the city has to comply with state and
  federal requirements, second the city has adopted the county’s
  requirements for development.

  Mr. Houston stated after listening to the concerns the K-rail stays as is and
  removes the requirement for Condition No. 60 and adds new Condition
  No. 74. And offline quickly speaking with the developer and making
  certain this type of language is okay.

  Mr. Burt stated they are happy with that condition, but with just one
  change the applicant shall provide clearance for all applicable oversight
  agencies.

  Page 9 of 16
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025

3
TRACT MAP ADMIN
CONT’D  Mr. Salinas stated if there were any violations then these agencies would
  be additional enforcement.

  Councilwoman Avalos asked the appellants if they are okay with this new
  addition?

  Mr. Morales is asking to make certain there is a permanent barrier on
  Adella. He is not comfortable with the new changes.

  Councilwoman Avalos asked City Attorney and City Manager regarding
  the incident that happened at Legacy High School, what are the options
  that the fire department can hold us accountable because of the limited
  access?

  Mr. Houston stated the fire department had approved the project in their
  review with the K-rail as is and it didn’t require that it have emergency
  access. The concept was that it would be a good feature to add for access
  both ways.

  Mr. Houston stated the appellants need to clarify which way they’re trying
  to sway.

  Councilwoman Avalos asked Mr. Morales as to which way they would
  want to sway.

  Mr. Morales stated they never said no to a modification of the K-rail. They
  don’t want anything that will keep traffic in and out, even for emergencies.

  Councilwoman Avalos asked even for emergencies basis?

  Council Member Hurtado explained he resides at the Thunderbird Villa,
  and it does not have a lot of access. Emergency vehicles never have a
  problem. He doesn’t mind having a permanent barrier.

  Councilwoman Avalos asked City Attorney if the fire department had
  anything to say regarding the limited access to Legacy High School.

  Mr. Salinas stated that the fire department did not require a gate or access
  through Adella onto the other side of the K-rail.

  Mr. Cervantes stated he saw the letter from the fire department regarding
  whether or not access was required but what is not clear is if the K-rail or
  its predicament was presented to the fire department.

  Page 10 of 16
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025
3
TRACT MAP ADMIN
CONT’D  Mr. Cervantes stated the city, nor the residents, do not have the
  unrestricted right to just say open the street because there are
  environmental documents in place.

  Mr. Burt stated the appellants have insisted that they wanted to keep the
  K-rail and now he is surprised the condition has changed. He stated that
  the applicant is willing to give a certain sum of money towards that future
  improvement. The original amount was $10,000 dollars.

  Council Member Hurtado stated the city needs to give a commitment to
  the community regarding something permanent.

  Mr. Houston stated the big decision before the City Council is this project
  going forward or not. The traffic flow is agreed be it K-rail or some other
  device will not be opened and what design that takes can be figured out
  separately.

  Mr. Burt stated another condition can be added. Condition 75 clarifies that
  the developer, the applicant will pay the city $10,000 dollars to be used for
  public works purposes or public improvements.

  Councilwoman Avalos asked Mr. Morales if they would be okay with that
  additional condition.

  Mr. Morales stated they would be okay with adding Condition 75.

  AMENDMENTS:

  Remove requirement on Condition No. 60. As part of the project, the
  applicant is required to replace the existing “K-rail” barrier near the
  intersection of Adella and Legacy Lane with an automated arm gate, or like
  device (Automated Unit) to allow emergency vehicle access and non-
  restricted access at designated times, as determined by the City. The
  Automated Unit’s design and installation shall be subject to the review and
  approval of the Director of Public Works and will be maintained and
  operated by the City.

  New Condition No. 74. Applicant shall provide clearance for all applicable
  oversight agencies (such as, Fire Department, AQMD, DTSC, and Regional
  Water Quality Control Board) of the project site to confirm site remediation
  and testing is adequate prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy for
  each phase of development.

  New Condition No. 75. Developer agrees to contribute the sum for $10,000
  for use by the City of South Gate for a public works project related to a
  permanent gate structure or any other project as the City may so deem.

  Page 11 of 16
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 27, 2025

RECESS  The City Council recessed at 10:53 p.m., and reconvened at 10:59 p.m.,
  with all Members of Council present.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE (NON-AGENDA
ITEMS)  Video not audible.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Council Member Avalos attended the Contract Cities Conference and the
  Memorial Service at South Gate Park.

  Council Member Hurtado has researched how to handle misinformation,
  but in our community it’s disinformation.

  Vice Mayor Barron explained his reason for not being present at the last
  Council Meeting. He had pre-scheduled trip to pick up his daughter from
  school and she is present tonight.

  Vice Mayor Barron thanked City Council for listening to the item that
  came before Council. It was a tough decision. He appreciates the efforts
  by City staff.

  Vice Mayor Barron was saddened to see signs in the back of the Council
  Chambers saying recall corrupt Council Members. He remembers back in
  2003 walking to recall true corruption.

  Mayor Davila attended the Contract Cities Conference and the Memorial
  Service at South Gate Park.

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 were approved by motion of
  Council Member Avalos and seconded by Council Member Rios.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes (recused from item 9); Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor
  Barron, yes; Mayor Davila, yes (recused from item 4).
4

ASSESSMENTS  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a. The Tweedy Mile Advisory Board’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year
  2025/26; and

  b. Resolution No. 2025-18-CC entitled Resolution of the City Council of
  the City of South Gate, California, declaring the City’s intention to
  levy and collect assessments for Fiscal Year 2025/26 for the Parking

LEVY AND COLLECT

BUSINESS LICENSE
ADMIN  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B & C during Consent
  Calendar:

  a. Amendment No. 1 to Contract No. 2024-96-AC with Hinderliter De
  Llamas & Associates (“Agreement”), through December 31, 2027, for
  Business License Administration and Business License Discovery/

  b. Appropriated $7,500 from the General Fund balance to expenditure

LANDSCAPING  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B, C, D & E during
  Consent Calendar:

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2025-34-CC) with Superior Pavement

  Thermoplastic Striping of Streets Citywide Project Phase II, City

  e. Notice of Exemption for the construction of the Thermoplastic

  directing the City Clerk to file it with the Los Angeles County

LAW ENFORCEMENT  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B, C & D during
  Consent Calendar:

  a. 5-year Lease Agreement (Contract No. 2025-35-CC) with Lease
  Servicing Center, Inc. dba NCL Government Capital (“NCL”) for the
  lease of one 2025 Ford Maverick vehicle to be used as a Parking

  b. Lease payments in the amount of $7,785 to be budgeted annually for

  c. Purchase Order Agreement with Commline Inc., for the purchase and
  installation of necessary emergency equipment and MDC to outfit the
  Parking Enforcement vehicle in the amount of $14,035; and

  d. Authorized the Mayor to execute the lease Agreement and any other
  documents that may be necessary to acquire the vehicles in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

  Consent Calendar:

  a. Authorized utilization of 2023 Homeland Security Grant Program

  b. Increased the Fiscal Year 2025/26 revenue projection in Account

  Grant) to $40,000; and

  c. Amended the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Law Enforcement Grants Fund
  Budget by appropriating $40,000 to Account Number 232-541-21-
  6204 (Law Enforcement Grants-Homeland Security Grant – Small
  Tools and Equipment); and

  d. Authorized the City Manager to execute the State Homeland Security
  Grant Program Subrecipient Agreement (Contract No. 2025-36-CC)
  for Grant Year 2023.

9
STREETS/SIDEWALKS/
LANDSCAPING  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a. Contract Change Order 2 to Contract No. 2023-66-CC with WGJ
